A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core method, and original experiments. All pages, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison; retained appendix material can be matched despite renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original DAVIS reconstruction experiments, quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–3, and appendix measurements of VRAM usage and sensitivity to stochasticity.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds GoPro deblurring, DAVIS/Pexels super-resolution comparisons, and a human perceptual study in Tables 4 and 7–9.

M1.justification: The original solver remains unchanged, but Appendix B.1 adds a substantive blind-deblurring extension. Algorithm 2 uses DeepDeblur pre-restoration to estimate a PSF, performs reconstruction, re-estimates the PSF, and performs a second reconstruction. This introduces degradation estimation and an additional model component beyond the known-operator procedure.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates DAVIS with known temporal and spatio-temporal degradations. v3 additionally evaluates blind and known deblurring on GoPro and super-resolution on high-frame-rate Pexels videos, substantially broadening data and degradation-knowledge coverage. Blind super-resolution and frame interpolation in Appendix B.2 are discussed without reported experiments.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated video-restoration comparators: DeepDeblur on GoPro in Table 4 and DiffIR2VR for super-resolution in Tables 7–8. The original CG, ADMM-TV, DPS, and DiffusionMBIR comparisons remain. FMA-Net and the SDx4 upscaler are mentioned through prior work, not independently evaluated.

E3.justification: Original DAVIS settings are retained. New protocols include GoPro blind restoration with randomly selected blur widths from 7–13 versus known degradation at width 13, resolution-matched patch reconstruction for the additional super-resolution comparison, and side-by-side human evaluation with 36 reported votes addressing reconstruction quality and temporal consistency. These are added evaluation designs, not revisions to the original experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix C.5 adds supplementary human validation of perceived reconstruction quality and temporal consistency. Existing analyses of CG updates, stochasticity control, the eta parameter, and VRAM usage are retained unchanged, including the relocated appendix visualizations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability estimates. The new human study supplies vote counts and preference shares, but adds no uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original numerical results are unchanged, including v2 Tables 4–5, now v3 Tables 5–6. New Tables 4 and 7–9 add substantial results. On DAVIS super-resolution, ours versus DiffIR2VR achieves PSNR 32.88 versus 30.51 and FVD 0.166 versus 0.212, but worse LPIPS, 0.089 versus 0.061. Pexels shows the same metric tradeoff. Table 9 reports 0.944 preference for ours on both questions. GoPro blind and known results use different blur settings and do not establish a matched-setting performance difference.

T1.justification: The existing mathematical formulation, linear-manifold assumptions, and DDS/Krylov reasoning are retained. Algorithm 2 specifies additional optimization steps for the blind extension, but introduces no new theoretical analysis, proof, or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The introduction's contribution list newly claims extensibility to blind restoration, and Section 3 points to its algorithm and experiments. The abstract, conclusion, and central claims about image diffusion priors, batch consistency, reconstruction quality, and speed remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive applicability qualifications absent from v2: PSF-estimation errors, the 256×256 resolution ceiling, reduced reliability under severe temporal degradation, and doubled sampling time for blind restoration. Appendix B.2 also discusses possible super-resolution and interpolation adaptations. New superiority interpretations in C.3–C.4 do not discuss the LPIPS disadvantage shown in their tables.

D1.justification: v3 identifies DeepDeblur as the pre-restoration component, supplies blind-extension pseudocode, documents patch reconstruction for resolution matching, identifies Pexels as an additional data source, and discloses doubled blind-sampling time. Existing preprocessing, hyperparameters, hardware information, and code/data availability statements are unchanged; implementation details for the additions remain limited.

R1.justification: v3 adds references concerning DeepDeblur/GoPro, DiffIR2VR, FMA-Net, latent diffusion, and RAFT to support the new comparisons and proposed extensions. This locally expands positioning relative to video-restoration research without revising the original DDS-based motivation or broader literature discussion.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v3 adds acknowledgments, updates the publication header, makes small wording and cross-reference edits, inserts the blind-extension appendix, and moves the previous Appendix B into an expanded Appendix C. This is localized restructuring rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adds GoPro Figure 8, Tables 4 and 7–9, and Algorithm 2 using the existing presentation style. Original figures remain visually unchanged; appendix figures and tables are relocated and renumbered. Layout changes are concentrated around these additions.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's DAVIS-only evidence, v3 provides a concrete blind-restoration extension, relevant video-restoration comparisons, additional datasets, and human preferences. Its explicit limitations also clarify applicability. These gains are tempered by sparse reporting of Pexels selection and human-study procedures, unmatched blind/known GoPro settings, and superiority wording that leaves the LPIPS disadvantage unexplained. The additions improve coverage and transparency, but support a limited overall quality gain.
